newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end mixed on uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end mixed on uncertainty.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mixed on Monday due to an uncertain short-term market trend, traders said.
The most active March 1997 contract ended at 20,190 yuan ($2,432) per tonne, down 60 yuan. It opened at an intra-day low of 20,000 and hit a high of 20,220.
December rose 140 to 20,400, January 60 to 20,310 and February 20 to 20,220, while April fell 70 to 20,190, May 80 to 20,200 and July 150 to 20,210.
Combined volume fell to 70,190 tonnes from 72,755.
Copper opened lower but short-covering and speculative buying pushed prices up from lows for most of the session.
Traders said the uncertain short-term market trend made many investors buy or sell for quick profits.
"Speculative buying from retail investors dominated today's trading and investors did not want to build large amounts of short positions," one trader said.
"Most contracts found strong psychological support at the 20,000-yuan level today," he added.
"Copper is likely to fall further on poor fundamentals until major positive news emerges," a second trader said.
Analysts expect copper to fall to the 20,000-yuan level in the next few days.
Aluminium ended down. December fell 40 to 13,800 yuan per tonne and January 50 to 13,950.
Combined volume fell to 110 tonnes from 290.
